Your browser does not support the video tag. Frederick (Rick) Zaplitny Obituary #With great sadness, we announce the sudden and peaceful passing of Rick Zaplitny on March 2, 2025 at the Dauphin Personal Care Home at the age of 78, with his wife Bev by his side.
Rick was born on August 7, 1946 in Dauphin and married the love of his life, Bev, in 1970. He earned his Chartered Accountant designation in 1973.
Rick spent nearly his entire life in Dauphin and was deeply connected with the community. In addition to raising a family with Bev and owning a successful business, he made countless contributions to the community. He served a term as town councilor and deputy mayor, was an active member of community service groups such as the Kinsmen, Masons and Shriners and was a past board member and Chair of the St. Paul’s Personal Care Home.
Beyond his local commitments, Rick dedicated many years to the Heart and Stroke Foundation of Manitoba, eventually serving as Chair. Having experienced heart-related health challenges himself, this cause was near and dear to him.
Rick enjoyed golfing, fishing, hunting, bowling and was a long-time Dauphin Kings season ticket holder. Later in life, Rick became a voracious reader and maintained his love for cribbage.
Above all, Rick was devoted to his family, raising Chris and Paula and sharing his love of sports, activities and travel while instilling in them the importance of education. Family trips across western Canada and many summers in Clear Lake will never be forgotten. Later in life, Rick and Bev found great joy in travelling to Bermuda and the Cayman Islands to visit their children, especially when grandchildren started to arrive.
Rick is survived by his loving wife, Bev; son Chris (Kathy); daughter Paula (Richard); grandchildren Rylan, Cade, Annabelle and Elisabeth; sister Gail White; brothers John (Linda) and Michael (Michelle); mother-in-law Kay Lysak; sisters-in-law Barb Mrozowich (Jerry) and Connie Neilipovitz (Bill) and numerous other extended family members. Rick was predeceased by his parents, Fred and Elizabeth Zaplitny (nee Koshey); his father-in-law John Lysak; his brother-in-law Gerry White; and his sister-in-law Susan Zaplitny.
The family is extremely grateful for the compassionate care provided by the staff at the Dauphin and Grandview hospitals, and the Dauphin Personal Care Home where Rick spent the last several months of his life.
A Celebration of Life was held for Rick on Monday, April 28, 2025 at 2:00 pm at the Sneath-Strilchuk Family Care Centre in Dauphin with Ryan Raffray officiating.
Should friends so desire, donations in memory of Rick may be made to the Heart and Stroke Foundation of Canada.
title: Remembering R.W. Bro. Rick Zaplitny

content:
The installation of the Worshipful Master and Officers of Vermillion Lodge No. 68 was a momentous occasion, held on May 23rd, 2026.
This year, the Parkland District joint installation of officers brought together three Brother Lodges:
Vermillion Lodge No. 68 (Dauphin, MB) – Installing WB Jake Rana as Worshipful Master. Prince of Wales Lodge No. 14 (Minnedosa, MB) – Installing Bro. Thedwinston Paris as Worshipful Master. Russell Lodge No. 62 (Russell, MB) – Installing RW Bro. Wes Osborne as Worshipful Master. The ceremony was attended by distinguished members of the Grand Lodge of Manitoba, lodge members, and their families and friends. We extend our warmest congratulations to WB Jake Rana and all the newly installed officers across the Parkland District. We look forward to a successful and inspiring year ahead of Masonic brotherhood, community dedication, and mutual improvement.
title: Installation of WB Jake Rana

Vermillion Lodge welcomes our new members Bro Scott Sylvester and Bernardo Pasco.
Taking the first step in Masonry is a significant commitment to self-improvement and brotherly love. We are honored to welcome them into the fraternity and look forward to supporting them on their journey.
title: Welcoming our new members

content:
The Holiday season has officially arrived in Dauphin!
On the evening of November 28th, members, friends, and families of Vermillion Lodge #68 gathered to enjoy the magic of the annual Dauphin Parade of Lights. It was wonderful to see our community come together under the winter stars to celebrate the spirit of the season.
Following the parade, the warmth continued back at the Lodge. We enjoyed a hearty, festive meal together, sharing stories and laughter. The highlight of the night was the fellowship found in our family games, where brothers and their loved ones competed in good spirits—a true reminder that the strength of our Lodge is found in the families that support us.
As we look toward the remainder of the year, we wish all our Brethren and the entire Dauphin community a very Merry Christmas and a season filled with peace and harmony.
Happy Holidays from the Worshipful Master, Officers, and Brethren of Vermillion Lodge #68!
title: A Festive Evening: Parade of Lights & Family Fellowship

content:
Vermillion Lodge No. 68 hosted a memorable Ladies’ Table Lodge, celebrating fellowship, tradition, and gratitude. The evening was guided by R.W. Bro. Rick Laronde, who served as Master of Ceremonies, ensuring a warm and engaging atmosphere throughout the event.
The Lodge was honoured by the presence of M.W. Bro. Rey Galapon, Grand Master, and R.W. Bro. Gord Greasley, Deputy Grand Master, whose attendance added distinction to the occasion.
The evening was shared by the Brethren and Wives of Vermillion Lodge, together with cherished guests and the Widows of our departed Brothers, who continue to hold a special place in the heart of the Lodge and its traditions. The event reflected the true spirit of Masonry—unity, respect, and appreciation for the ladies who support and strengthen the Craft.
title: Ladies Table Lodge

title: Masonic Links

content:
Making Good Men Better. #Freemasonry is the oldest and largest fraternal organization in the world. Its members share a common goal of helping each other become better men. Its body of knowledge and system of ethics is based on the belief that each man has a responsibility to improve himself while being devoted to his family, faith, country, and fraternity.
Its roots go back centuries and its members are diverse: high profile leaders, physicians, construction workers, farmers…and maybe you.
Ancient…and modern. #We’re united by three ancient and fundamental principles—brotherly love, charity and truth—that are made relevant to the 21st century through the personal development, good works and social connections available to our members in the 550+ lodges across Ontario.
Great benefits…for you and the world. #Freemasonry offers much to its members—the opportunity to grow, the chance to make a difference and the means to build a better world for our children. It offers the chance to socialize and work with men who have the same values and ideals.
We strengthen and improve our character by learning and practicing basic virtues of fraternal love, charity, and truth. Our principles extend far beyond our interactions with each other, and we strive to apply them to our daily lives.
And there’s so much more. #It’s easy to learn about Masons—starting with the pages of this website. Need more details? Looking for a Mason in your community to share his personal perspective?
